_doc: Mutable campaign state. The driver reads it to decide whether to start a cycle; the cycle updates it at the end. A fresh session with no context can resume the campaign from this file alone.
last_cycle_outcome: P01 done — hardware re-baseline on CUDA; champions re-measured, sota.json and campaign.yaml updated

history.note: Port MacBook/MPS -> Windows/RTX 4060 (CUDA). 12 runs, 3 seeds x (H35 connectome, H30 microns, H30 mouse, H35 mouse). All champions re-measured; every seed bit-identical (sigma = 0). Also fixed: CRLF broke the frozen manifest; the guard hook was inert on Windows; audit.py pooled runs across devices and called the frozen scorer with the wrong signature; the driver watchdog could not kill native Windows processes.

machine: Windows 10 laptop, NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (CUDA), Git Bash
notes: P01 done 2026-08-09 on the new machine; the campaign may now run cycles. Two things a resuming session must know. (1) The champion pipelines are DETERMINISTIC here: they take a seed but never draw from it, so seeds 42/123/999 give bit-identical positions and sigma = 0. A Welch CI built on those seeds is degenerate (SE = 0), so a verdict needs delta > screen_delta_pp AND the floored PROTOCOL CI; audit.py emits significance.<ds>.degenerate when this applies. (2) microns costs 3240 s/run here (706 s on MPS), so a 3-seed screen is ~3.2 h and a 5-seed confirm ~5.3 h; max_cycle_wall_clock_h was raised 6 -> 10 and driver CYCLE_TIMEOUT_S 21600 -> 36000 so cycles are not killed mid-confirm. Queue item P02 (priority 1) asks whether the inert seeds can be dropped for deterministic variants, which would cut a cycle from ~8.5 h to ~2.5 h. IF THIS CHECKOUT IS MOVED AGAIN: set hardware_rebaseline_done=false, update `machine` and environment.device_tag, and re-run P01 — sota.json is machine-specific (see autoresearch/PORTING.md).
